reasoning: iter-053: switch all 4 strided dispatches in tile_assign (bbox/scatter/precompute/cull) to block-chunked, rolling out the iter-051/052 pattern to the remaining hot path. The cull_stripe was the highest-impact: it wrote keep_mask[p] (1 byte/pair) at strided positions p, p+W, p+2W with W=10 — every 64 B cache line of keep_mask was simultaneously written by ALL workers, causing maximum cross-core line invalidation per store. Block-chunked dispatch makes each worker own a contiguous keep_mask span. Result: sum_total 306.6 -> 255 ms (-17%, -51 ms / 30 frames). Stage breakdown: tile_assign 53 -> 25 ms (-53%, the false-sharing on the byte mask was catastrophic); project 87 -> 69 (extra ~3 ms beyond iter-052's gain, likely from less LSU contention in the warm pool); blend/sort unchanged. PSNR identical (min 60.34, mean 63.26). p50 frame time now 8.64 ms — first time consistently below 10 ms. 3-trial confirmation: 258/314/254 (314 is a known system noise outlier — typical of one in ~10 runs). The blocked dispatch pattern is THE highest-impact win in this optimization run so far, and the lesson generalises: any per-element output array with byte/few-byte stores MUST be block-chunked, never strided.
